title: C266 — Right-hand footwell lamp
introduction:
I read the right-hand footwell lamp's connector row by row, rather than letting the familiar housing shape do the thinking. The red-light function has different gauge and terminal entries from the remaining functions—a useful reminder that matching sockets need not have matching details behind them. Start with the identity table, match the drawing's cavity label, then follow the whole row across.

This is a connector-reading and parts-reference guide. Physical access, viewing side, probing conditions, test limits and replacement methods are outside its scope. The gauge convention and meanings of Box, Cols, Size and Used are unspecified. Preserve the complete ambient-lighting configuration wording; it describes the listed function without confirming which equipment is fitted to a particular car.

edits.why: I use the broad left-hand projection and lower-right hooked outline to recognize the drawing's displayed orientation. Each printed cavity label leads to the corresponding Cavity row below. Those visual landmarks help navigate the map, but they do not identify a physical terminal-side or wire-side view or establish a connector-release movement.

The row ties a cavity to its Circuit Number, wire Color, Gauge, complete Function and Terminal Part Number. Read the gauge and terminal fields individually: the red-light entry differs from the remaining entries in both fields. Wire Color and the light color named in Function serve different purposes. Keep the ambient-lighting configuration qualifier with each function, and do not turn a listed role into a fault conclusion.

The kit entry, Service Part and Engineering Shell form the parts cross-reference. Its pigtail characteristics describe the listed service item, while the pin-assignment rows retain their own circuit details. I do not substitute the pigtail Gauge for a circuit-row Gauge. The Image field names an asset; this table does not teach connector replacement, terminal installation or splicing.
